text.en:
Archaeologists dug a mound near a river. Under the soil they found straight streets, brick houses and drains.
"This was a city," said the leader. "People lived here more than four thousand years ago."

Early people first hunted animals and gathered fruits. Later they learnt farming, kept animals and lived in villages. Mehrgarh is one of the earliest farming villages in South Asia.
The Harappan or Indus Valley civilisation was one of the first in the world. It flourished around 2600 to 1900 BCE in the Indus river region. Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira, Lothal and Rakhigarhi are important sites.
The cities were well planned, with straight streets, burnt-brick houses, wells and covered drains. Mohenjo-daro has the Great Bath.
People farmed wheat and barley, made pots, beads and tools, and traded with distant lands, using seals and standard weights.
The Harappan script has not been read yet, so we learn mostly from digging up things: seals, beads, pots, toys and ruins.
Early people hunted and gathered. Later they learnt farming and settled in villages.
The Indus Valley civilisation was one of the first in the world. It flourished about four thousand years ago.
Its cities, such as Harappa and Mohenjo-daro, had straight streets, brick houses and covered drains.
People traded using seals and weights. Their script is not yet read, so we learn from objects.

problem.en: What shows that Harappan cities were well planned?

text.en: Streets ran straight and crossed at right angles.
Houses were built of burnt bricks and had drains.
So the cities were carefully planned.

prompt.en: A friend asks how we know about the Harappans when we cannot read their writing. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: We learn from things dug up: seals, pots, beads, tools and ruins.
Archaeologists study these to understand how people lived.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking we can learn only from writing.

points.en: People moved from hunting to farming.
Harappan cities were planned, with drains and brick houses.
We learn about them from archaeological finds.
